rv.q: Simply put, it's a bold and interesting choice to do Chekhov in a factory, but it's not enough.
The production flags badly in pace as it sputters to its ending, beginning to confuse the depiction of tedium with dramatic listlessness.
But that's also why this production stands among the best I've seen.

cn.t: Critics praise this Uncle Vanya for its strong cast and inventive factory setting, which brings fresh perspective to Chekhov's tragicomedy of unhappiness and suffocation in the Russian countryside.
